newsitem.title: USA: Miami fails to approve budget, meets again next week.
newsitem.headline: Miami fails to approve budget, meets again next week.

text.p: Miami's city commission, trying to thrash out a budget to rescue it from financial disaster, met for more than three hours on Monday without reaching agreement, a city spokeswoman said.
The commission will meet again next Monday, Charlene Watkins said.
It must present its budget by January 3 to the state emergency board appointed by Florida Governor Lawton Chiles to oversee the scandal-plagued city's recovery from bankruptcy.
Miami, a city of about 350,000 people, faces a $68 million budget gap in the fiscal year ending September 31.
Its financial plight emerged after a corruption and bribery scandal that saw city manager Cesar Odio and longtime commissioner Miller Dawkins lose their jobs.

"The manager (Ed Marquez) has been working on this all weekend," Watkins said. "It's a coordination thing. There was no conflict -- it was all very collegiate. There will be another meeting on Monday, January 30."

Mayor Joe Carollo has laid out a budget plan that used wage and pension concessions, grants, cost cuts and fee hikes to balance the budget without raising property taxes, garbage fees or selling land. It consists of $17.57 million of new one-time revenues, $15.76 million of recurring new revenues, and $37.8 million in recurring savings.

Carollo said earlier this month that his plan would give the city breathing room to seek other new revenue sources and expand its property tax base, but the initial reaction from the emergency board was cool.
Rating agencies have already lowered Miami's bond status to non-investment grade.

Some relief came to the city last Friday when police agreed to $15 million in wage and benefit concessions over the next two years, joining three other unions in approving concessions that will save it $25 million over two years.
The emergency board has given the commission a March deadline for coming up with five-year fiscal recovery plan.
